title: Hom bijection for the two affine-module tensor operations
statement: Let f:U→X be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], put A=f_*O_U, and let R be direct image to A-modules and S restriction of A-modules to O_X-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use the canonical inverse-image modules and ring adjunction unit [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. Let B be a sheaf of commutative rings on U, b:O_U→B, t:f⁻¹A→B and ε:B→O_U, with tε equal to the ring adjunct of id_A. Let P and H be functors on module sheaves with object equalities pobj:P(G)=B⊗_(f⁻¹A) f⁻¹G and hobj:H(G)=O_U⊗_B P(G), using sheafified sectionwise scalar extension [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let κ:P followed by restriction along b ≅ S followed by tensorPullback(f), and γ:S followed by tensorPullback(f)→H. Use the canonical tensor-pullback adjunction [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] and its unit u. Require that, for all G,V,g, pobj(κ⁻¹(u_(SG)(g)))=θ_t(1⊗η_G(g)), and for all G,W,p, hobj(γ_G(κ_G(p)))=θ_ε(1⊗p), where θ denotes the module sheafification unit. Let β:id→H followed by R be a natural transformation whose image under S is the ordinary tensor-pullback adjunct of γ_G. Then for every A-module sheaf G and O_U-module sheaf F, the function Hom(HG,F)→Hom(G,RF), a↦β_G followed by R(a), is bijective. No affineness or quasi-coherence is assumed.

proof.text: For each algebra module G and structure-sheaf module F, transport Hom(HG,F) along hobj and apply the scalar-extension Hom bijection for ε, obtaining Hom(PG,Res_ε F). Transport along pobj and apply the scalar-extension Hom bijection for t to obtain Hom(f⁻¹G,Res_t Res_ε F).

Apply the inverse-image module Hom bijection to identify the last Hom set with Hom(G,f_*(Res_t Res_ε F)). The scalar map is η_A followed by f_*(t ε). Since t ε is the inverse ring adjunct of the identity of A, the ring Hom equivalence identity identifies this scalar map with the identity of A. Hence the final module is RF.

The section formula for the composite Hom bijection is a evaluated on θ_ε(1⊗θ_t(1⊗η_G(g))). The hP formula expresses the inner section as pobj applied to κ inverse applied to the ordinary tensor-pullback unit. The hH formula expresses the outer section as hobj applied to γκ on that section. Cancel both equality transports and κκ inverse; this is a evaluated on γ applied to the ordinary pullback unit. By hβ and the ordinary adjunction Hom formula it is β_G followed by R(a). Thus the indicated function is the composite of the bijections in the preceding steps and is bijective.
